name: os-windows-legacy
comment: Windows NT 4.0 through Windows 8.1 and Windows Server 2003 through 2012 R2, and the KBs no input records a product for: os/server-2008, os/server-2012, os/windows-7 and os/windows-8-1, and with them the os/windows and os/windows-server notice lines, which render no listing and collect the pre-Windows-10 one-offs. Windows is the one family split further, by OS line, because a line is a series boundary under os/ and the family is too large for one shard. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: dotnet-framework
comment: the .NET Framework monthly line, in 22 series, one per host OS build: dotnetframework/windows-10/1607 through 22h2, dotnetframework/windows-11/21h2 through 26h1, dotnetframework/microsoft-server/2022, /23h2 and /hci, and the bare dotnetframework line. The servicing path spells the product unhyphenated; the group name follows msuc-targets.json. They stay in one shard because splitting a family cannot make a series smaller -- it can only make one reachable from two shards. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: dotnet-runtime
comment: .NET Core and .NET 5 and newer, in 11 series: dotnet/net-5 through net-10, dotnet/net-core-3-1 and developer/update. net-8 and newer render a listing, so a seed pulls the whole line -- that is how KB5038352 (.NET 8.0.5), expired in the Update Catalog, comes back. net-7 and older render none, so every KB is named. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: office
comment: Office and SharePoint: office, office/hotfix and office/update/2026. Microsoft serves the SharePoint articles from the office product, so they are seeded here rather than in a shard of their own -- the family a KB is seeded under is the one its article is served from. Grouped by product family, not by product version as msuc-targets.json is: a seed pulls its whole series listing, shards do not share what a run has already stored, so a series two shards can both reach is fetched twice -- and family is the coarsest key that keeps a series whole.

name: exchange
comment: Exchange Server, in 10 series: exchange/server and its hotfix, troubleshooting and update lines, and exchange/update. The Update Catalog does not carry Exchange at all, so the article is the only record of its update and every KB is named rather than reached from a seed. Grouped by product family like the rest of this file, though the reason the other groups have does not apply here: nothing expands, so no shard can duplicate another's work and the split is free. Family keeps it consistent with the groups where it is not.
